payload.question_text: At a business, an employee uploads a scanned receipt and needs the system to find where the printed words are located before extracting expense fields. The computer vision technology that finds text locations in the image is ___.

parts.text: The computer vision technology that finds text locations in an image is

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The image's text locations would not be named precisely.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Use OCR for text locations; information extraction is broader and speech recognition works with audio.

payload.explanation: OCR is the computer vision technology for identifying text locations in images.

payload.question_text: A workplace AI agent receives text-format information and must respond aloud to an employee. Reconstruct the statement describing how it produces the spoken response from the pieces.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The source and result are mixed up.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Keep text-format information before the audible signal.

payload.correct_answer: Text-to-speech converts text-format information into an audible signal

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The source is text-format information and the result is an audible signal.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Text-to-speech is speech synthesis: it converts text-format information into an audible signal. Speech recognition works in the opposite direction, converting spoken audio into text. Identify the input and output direction before arranging the pieces.

payload.explanation: Text-to-speech is a form of speech synthesis that converts text-format information into an audible signal. Speech recognition is different: it converts spoken audio into text. To solve similar questions, identify the input and output direction—text to audio means text-to-speech; speech to text means speech recognition.
